purpose: Historical Gateway application overload observations, including source HTTP admission rejection; not an isolated JDBC lock-cost experiment.
conclusions: HTTP_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT is a source HTTP admission timeout, not evidence of JDBC correctness failure.
The original workflow failure statuses and all numerical observations are preserved below; they are not retroactively relabelled as successful jobs.
Use these observations for application completion/rejection rates, latency and carrier-availability behavior under the recorded limits.
Do not use CPU/success, successful throughput, or these whole-Gateway differences to isolate lock-strategy costs. The earlier lock-adoption interpretation is withdrawn.

metric_semantics.summary: Median of four per-JVM values; p99 columns are medians of per-JVM p99, not pooled quantiles.
metric_semantics.cpu: Whole-process CPU / successful HTTP requests; stress numerator includes failed requests and backups.
metric_semantics.cv: Sample standard deviation / arithmetic mean of four per-cell RPS values.
metric_semantics.pairing: Same repetition number on same hosted job, sequential not simultaneous; not paired same-time measurements.
metric_semantics.pins: Zero JFR VirtualThreadPinned events does not exclude carrier blocking inside JNI.
metric_semantics.host_variability: Large final wall-throughput variation is observed; disk/host contention cause was not instrumented and remains unproven.

runs.flat_definition: Replace three synchronized(conn) scopes with synchronized(conn.getDatabase()), retaining recursion depth.

callback.notification: single background-process completion callback; REST polling internally
